issues.justification: The slang 'редиска' (a lousy person) is rendered literally and the pun on fenya jargon is lost; 'radish' makes no sense to English viewers, and the later joke (Fedya's dictionary) is undermined.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк... Я злой и страшный серый волк, я в поросятах знаю толк.
issues.translation_quote: I'm a big, bad, fearsome wolf, and piglets are my specialty.
issues.justification: The song and rhyme are lost; 'specialty' sounds odd and loses the rhyme and the playfulness of the nursery song.

issues.source_quote: В поезде я с полки упал... Обзовись! - Век воли не видать!
issues.translation_quote: Swear to it! - May I never be free again!
issues.justification: 'Век воли не видать' is a thieves' oath, repeatedly used. Here it is rendered as a plain oath, while later 'Лошадью ходи, век воли не видать!' becomes 'I swear!', so the recurring marker is inconsistent and loses the criminal flavor.

issues.translation_quote: Dinner is served! Sit down and stuff your faces, please.
issues.justification: Fine, but the 'Кушать подано' / 'Нашел фраера' butler-like comic contrast is partly kept; main failures lie elsewhere.

issues.translation_quote: Move the horse! The horse, you fool!
issues.justification: In English chess the piece is a knight; 'horse' sounds odd, though partly tolerable as slang.

issues.source_quote: Эй, гражданина! Ты туда не ходи, ты сюда ходи, а то снег башка попадет - совсем мертвый будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Hey, citizen! Don't go there. Come this way, or snow hit head— you be completely dead!
issues.justification: The pseudo-Central-Asian pidgin joke is preserved only half; the rhyme was added, shifting the effect.

issues.translation_quote: I'll tear your mouth off! ... I'll gouge your eyes out
issues.justification: Fixed threats are conveyed, but 'Пасть порву' as 'tear your mouth off' is a calque; 'rip your jaw off' or similar would be more natural. Minor naturalness issue repeated throughout.
The joke 'Кто же его посадит?' pun on sit/imprison is rendered as 'Who'd lock him up?', which only partly works.
